title: See CLI tests and timed scripts and infrastructure results in Intent

intentCoverage.report:
## Dough Intent Coverage: Caught

**Story and revision.** SEED-109#complete-test-inventory-and-script-proof, Key example 3: "When a Bash file or Node.js case fails and reports a duration, that outcome and duration contribute to its file and the group." Plan 085-unify-tooling-test-proof. Revision 10ac6ef354e15643409df4e7e9e9da3524e7a2a1 (branch claude/see-cli-tests-and-timed-scripts-and-infrastructu).

**Promise and expected behavior.** The Node CI proof reporter (`scripts/ci/node-test-report.mjs`) counts each leaf case as one check, with its outcome and duration. A suite or parent test that fails only because a subtest failed must not add a check. The failing subtest is already counted with its time, so an extra untimed "failed" check would inflate the file's and group's failed and untimed counts.

**Fault.** In `check()` in `scripts/ci/node-test-report.mjs`, the parent branch dropped the `subtestsFailed` exclusion:
`return failed && data.details.error.failureType !== 'subtestsFailed'` became `return failed`.
No fixture or assertion was changed.

**Fixture and maintained assertion.** Fixture: `outcomes.test.mjs` in `scripts/ci/ci-proof-outcomes-node.test.mjs`. Its `describe('suite')` contains a failing `it('fails inside')` and a passing `it('passes inside')`. The fixtures run through `scripts/ci/node-test.mjs` with `CI_PROOF_NODE_REPORT_DIR` set. Assertion: `assert.deepEqual(outcomes('outcomes'), [...9 entries...])` at line 114 of the test "a Node report gives one check per test case from the directly selected files, named after the running package script".

**Run observations.**
- Scratch checkout: a detached `git worktree` at 10ac6ef354 under /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/25b13128/tmp/ic-scratch, with 0 changes before the probe. Root dependencies were installed with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter .` because the first run failed when the `yaml` package was missing. The checkout stayed clean afterward because `node_modules` is ignored.
- Focused command, run in the Nix shell with Node v26.13.0: `CURSOR_DEV=true nix develop -c node --test --test-name-pattern='a Node report gives one check' scripts/ci/ci-proof-outcomes-node.test.mjs`
- Baseline: the selected test passed (1 pass, 0 fail; the test took 267 ms).
- With the fault: the selected test failed at line 114 with `ERR_ASSERTION` from `deepStrictEqual`. The actual list had a 10th entry `['failed', false]`, an extra untimed failed check, after the expected 9. That is the intended assertion failing on the changed behavior.
- Reach and behavior, checked separately: with the fault still in place, a probe file holding only the same failing and passing suite was run through `node-test.mjs` with reporting on. It produced 3 lines: the timed failed leaf, the timed passed leaf, and an extra `{"status":"failed",...}` with no `seconds` for the suite. So the fault produced the wrong check on the suite-parent path.
- Restoration: the file was restored with `git checkout` from an EXIT trap. Afterward `git status --porcelain` showed 0 entries and `git diff --quiet HEAD` reported clean. The same focused command passed again (1 pass, 247 ms). The scratch worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove --force` and pruned.
- The execution checkout was never edited, stashed, reset or switched. When checked after the probe, it showed three staged deletions of the SEED-109 seed and the plan 085 files. This probe did not make them; they appear to come from the caller's concurrent wrap-up.

**Note.** This fixture covers a suite that fails because of a subtest. It does not cover a plain `test()` parent that fails only because of a subtest, which goes through the nesting-based parent detection. That branch was not probed here.

**Costs.**
- **Test runtime:** measured. The test runner reported the selected test at 267 ms at baseline, 286 ms with the fault and 247 ms after restoration. The whole runs (`duration_ms`) took 335 ms, 339 ms and 302 ms. The wall clock including Nix shell startup was about 1.2 s per run.
- **Human effort:** unavailable. No human took part in the run, and there is no separate measure of human time.
- **Agent effort:** unavailable. There is no token or tool-time meter that can be cited separately. About 12 tool calls were made; this is a count of operations, not a measure of effort.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 109261 ms (measured), from 1794154317061 to 1794154426322 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
